text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Government reaffirms commitment to euro single currency, says may delay some of its economic programme if the outcome of an audit around July 20 shows public finances in bad state.
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin called at Le Bourget Paris Air Show for European defence industry alliances, said supports plans to merge Aerospatiale and Dassault.
-- Commercial court to rule today on sale of 24.6 percent stake in holding Artemis by the CDR -- holding company involved in hiving off Credit Lyonnais assets -- to another state holding company.
-- Publicis stakeholder Michele Bleustein-Blanchet to sell her 20 percent stake in firm.
-- Eurotunnel creditor banks not expecting shareholders to reject financial restructuring plan which will be put to them on July 10, banking sources say.
LA TRIBUNE
-- "G8" industrialised nations' summit in Denver underlined the difference between Europe and the United States regarding unemployment.
-- Moulinex chairman Pierre Blayau calls in an interview calls for a defence of European industry against "dumping" of cheap products, notably from Asia.
-- Employers' federation (CNPF) leader Jean Gandois says a shift to a 35-hour working week without wage cuts would be a serious mistake.
-- Eurocopter chairman Jean-Francois Bigay says in an interview expects to set up production lines for the NH90 in 1998.
-- Heads of small and medium-sized firms sceptical on Jospin programme, notably on employment.
L'AGEFI
-- U.S. and British bond brokers increase Paris-based activities ahead of a European single currency.
LE PARISIEN

-- Losses and costs of Credit Lyonnais bailout estimated at more than 160 billion francs, including 102.8 billion in losses and 60 billion in continuing and future loan financing payments, according to a report sent to Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn by the EPFR holding company involved in Credit Lyonnais restructuring.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Former Communist Party leader Charles Fiterman calls in an interview for a partial privatisation of Air France and France Telecom.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- As Air Show ends, French government leaves privatisation route uncharted, Jospin did not make commitments on privatisations in defence industry.
